headline: SILVER CRASHES TO 2026 YEAR-TO-DATE LOW AT $53.89; GOLD RETESTS $4,000 FLOOR AHEAD OF FOMC
snippet: Silver broke below $54 for the first time in 2026 on Friday, October 23, closing at $53.89 — a year-to-date low down roughly 55% from January's all-time high above $120 — as crude oil's surge to multi-month highs stoked inflation concerns and reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady at its October 28 FOMC meeting. Gold also fell, briefly touching $3,991 before settling near $4,001 — testing the $4,000 psychological floor for the first time in three months. Silver was the worst-performing precious metal on the week (down 6.43% per Frank Holmes), and with the gold-silver ratio near 73 and both metals under pressure, the October 28 FOMC decision is now the most critical near-term catalyst for precious metals investors this quarter.

headline: MAJOR BROKER DUMPS AGNICO EAGLE, BARRICK AND NEWMONT TO HOLD — ALL THREE GOLD MAJORS CUT SAME DAY
snippet: Freedom Broker downgraded all three of the largest publicly-traded gold miners — Agnico Eagle, Barrick Gold, and Newmont — from Buy to Hold simultaneously, citing weaker near-term earnings expectations, ongoing operational challenges, and limited room for further share price appreciation at current gold levels. Gold mining stocks fell broadly on the session, tracking a 1.4% drop in spot bullion. For retail investors holding junior gold equities, simultaneous multi-name downgrades on senior producers typically signal a risk-off rotation out of the entire gold equity complex — juniors and mid-tiers often get compressed disproportionately in the days following major-house cuts on the sector's benchmark names.

headline: COPPER FALLS TO FIVE-WEEK LOW AT $14,089 AS LME WAREHOUSE STOCKS CLIMB FOR FOURTH STRAIGHT DAY
snippet: Three-month LME copper fell 1.8% to $14,089 per metric tonne — a five-week low — as exchange-monitored warehouse inventory posted a fourth consecutive daily increase, building a near-term demand softening narrative that has erased a meaningful portion of September's record near $14,875/t. A tentative labour agreement at BHP's largest Chilean copper mine eased one supply-side risk, though two unions representing 709 workers walked off the job at Antofagasta's Centinela mine, partially offsetting that relief. The October 28 FOMC meeting and any signal on US tariff policy remain the dominant macro triggers for the next sustained directional move in copper — a metal that has fragmented into regional pricing regimes following CME's recent admission that one global benchmark is no longer sufficient.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACT PRICE BREAKS 2007 RECORD AT $96.50/LB — SPOT HOLDS AT $89.63
snippet: The long-term uranium contract price closed September 2026 at $96.50 per pound, surpassing the previous record of $95 set in 2007 and marking the first time the term price has exceeded its prior cycle peak. The spot price held at $89.63 at month-end — below the term price, an inversion that signals utilities are paying a premium for multi-year supply security even as equity markets remain skeptical, with the VanEck Uranium and Nuclear ETF (NLR) down 16.4% year-to-date. For junior uranium developers, a term price above $90 means off-take contracts at economics-positive levels remain achievable, even as equity financing for project development stays difficult in the current risk-off environment.

headline: BLACK MAMMOTH METALS SECURES NEVADA DRILL PERMIT, EXTENDS MUSTANG GOLD TARGET ZONE SOUTH
snippet: Black Mammoth Metals announced it has extended the main mineralized target zone at its Mustang Gold and Silver property in Nevada southward — enlarging the drill-ready footprint — while simultaneously securing the permit required to commence drilling. Nevada's Battle Mountain and Walker Lane trends have produced several significant gold-silver discoveries in recent years, and the permit milestone removes the final regulatory gating item ahead of first-hole mobilization, setting up a near-term news catalyst for a junior explorer operating in one of the world's most mining-friendly jurisdictions at a time when $4,000 gold improves the economics of even modest discoveries.

headline: USA RARE EARTH DOWN 74% FROM PEAK — IS THE RESHORING THESIS STILL A ONCE-IN-A-GENERATION BET?
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis published October 22 examines whether USA Rare Earth — down 74% from its October 2025 peak and 15% year-to-date — remains a compelling domestic supply-chain play or has crossed into value-trap territory. The piece weighs the structural case for US rare earth self-sufficiency, including the company's pending $2.8 billion Serra Verde acquisition in Brazil, its milestone-based government funding structure, and a CEO transition, against the binary execution risks facing a pre-revenue company. With MP Materials also down 6% in recent sessions and Critical Metals declining 3%, the rare earth equity sector is in broad retreat even as Western governments maintain reshoring commitments — a divergence that defines the investment thesis debate.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO AT 73, ECONOMY 'TIPPY': TECHNICAL ANALYSIS MAPS SUPPORT LEVELS THROUGH FOMC WEEK
snippet: GoldSeek's Technical Scoop argues that recent weak US jobs data has shifted the macro narrative from soft-landing certainty to something more fragile — and that gold's failure to hold gains despite deteriorating employment data suggests the metal is being sold alongside equities in a broad de-risking trade rather than for fundamental reasons. The piece maps key support levels for gold and silver into the October 28 FOMC event and notes that the gold-silver ratio near 73 represents one of the higher readings of the 2025–2026 cycle. Historically, an elevated gold-silver ratio sustained through a Fed pivot or pause has preceded sharp silver outperformance — making the post-FOMC reaction in silver one of the more technically significant setups for precious metals investors right now.

headline: LME COPPER STOCKS AT FIVE-WEEK HIGH: GENUINE DEMAND SLOWDOWN OR TARIFF-DRIVEN INVENTORY SHIFT?
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis examines whether the current four-day build in LME copper warehouse inventory represents a genuine demand slowdown from China — potentially the first since Beijing's September stimulus package — or a tariff-driven repositioning of physical metal out of Comex warehouses and back into the LME system. The distinction matters materially for junior copper developers: if the inventory build is structural, it signals softening end-demand that would pressure the project economics case; if it is tariff-driven arbitrage, the LME price is temporarily overstating availability. CME's own recent statement that a single global copper benchmark is no longer effective has made this interpretation question more consequential for anyone running a copper-project feasibility model.

headline: SILVER INSTITUTE FORECASTS 67-MILLION-OUNCE SUPPLY DEFICIT IN 2026 — PRICE SLIDE DEFIES FUNDAMENTALS
snippet: The Silver Institute's 2026 outlook projects a 67 million ounce supply deficit — one of the largest annual deficits in the institute's recorded history — driven by sustained industrial demand growth from solar panels, EVs, and electronics outpacing mine supply gains. The disconnect between a record structural shortfall and a price at 2026 lows represents one of the more striking anomalies in commodity markets: silver closed Friday at a year-to-date low of $53.89, roughly 55% below January's all-time high. Money Metals' analysis traces the divergence to Fed rate-hike fears, dollar strength, and forced liquidation in futures markets — and maps prior deficit-vs-price disconnects to assess where and when a fundamental re-rating has historically arrived.

headline: ZACKS PICKS FIVE GOLD STOCKS FOR GROWTH AMID SECTOR PRESSURE — FRANCO-NEVADA AND CENTERRA AMONG NAMES
snippet: A Zacks analysis identifies five gold mining stocks positioned for growth despite broad sector selling pressure: Franco-Nevada, Centerra Gold, Novagold, Northern Dynasty, and Dakota Gold. The selection prioritizes companies with strong balance sheets, lower-than-sector-average cost structures, or near-term production and exploration catalysts that the analyst believes the market has not yet priced. The piece provides a counterpoint to Freedom Broker's same-week downgrade of the three largest gold producers, and implicitly argues that the selloff in senior names has created entry points in select mid-tier and royalty-streaming vehicles for investors willing to look past FOMC-week volatility. The distinction between seniors (high fixed costs, large hedged positions) and royalty names (no operating cost exposure) is a recurring theme in Zacks' sectoral analysis.
